To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and applied a procedure that combines the power of two‐dimensional (2D) electrophoresis with the power of peptide mass fingerprinting to identify and catalogue proteins expressed by human breast cancer cells.

1) the database of proteins expressed in breast carcinoma cells is now updated; 2) Triton X‐ 114 solubilized membrane proteins can be isolated by using either carrier ampholytes or pH gradients in the first dimension, but the latter results in a lower recovery of proteins; 3) the mass spectrometric procedure is now fully automated and is used to identify proteins from 2‐DE gel maps.

1) a 2‐DE gel database has been constructed for the breast carcinoma cell MDA‐MB‐231; and 2) a novel protein has been identified in the breast carcinoma MDA‐MB 231 cell line and assigned to a Mr/pI locus in the database.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a two‐dimensioned gel map of human breast carcinoma proteins and their identification.
identifying and characterising proteins expressed in human breast cancer cells and we have now assigned Mr/pI locii to 34 proteins.

the identification of new membrane proteins expressed by MDA‐MB 231 cells, the identification of proteins in the Triton X114 fraction using a combination of 2‐DE and RP‐HPLC and the comparison of the two‐dimensional protein databases of MCF‐7 and MDA‐MB‐231 cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

carrier ampholytes are more effective than immobilised pH gradients at resolving membrane proteins in the first dimension, and that the use of in‐gel trypsin digestion, RP‐HPLC and electrospray mass spectrometry is an effective method for identifying proteins from two‐dimensional gels.
the use of carrier‐ampholyte‐based IEF in the first dimension for the separation of membrane proteins in 2‐DE is superior to the use of immobilised pH gradients.

the use of immobilised pH gradients for the first dimension in 2‐DE is superior to carrier ampholytes, and that the use of 0.2‐mm ID capillary column RP‐HPLC for peptide mapping prior to electrospray ionization — ion trap — MS is an excellent approach for protein identification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
34 proteins from MDA MB231 cells have been identified, 29 of these being cytoplasmic in nature and five membrane associated.

the 2‐DE gel map of the human breast carcinoma cell line MDA‐MB‐231 is now complete for the 34 proteins identified in our previous study, plus nine additional cytoplasmic and three additional Triton X‐ 114 soluble proteins.
we have now mapped the Mr/pI locii of 35 proteins in the 2‐DE gel database of MDA‐MB 231 cells and have also identified a protein, previously represented in EST databases, as a membrane protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we now have a database for 35 cytoplasmic and membrane proteins from MCF7 and MDA‐MB‐231 breast carcinoma cells, which will be a valuable tool for proteomic studies of breast cancer.
the use of carrier‐ampholyte based IEF in the first dimension of 2‐DE can improve the recovery of membrane proteins.
the combination of 2‐DE and RP‐HPLC peptide mapping with mass spectrometry provides a rapid, sensitive and reliable means of identifying proteins in a complex mixture.
